rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Results sections (Figures 4-5) describe the authors' own Arduino/soil-moisture-sensor prototype, with sensed moisture data shown in Figure 4 and a bench set-up in Figure 5; the LED glows while the pump runs until the stored moisture threshold is reached.
rows.notes: The paper is essentially a design/prototype description of an IoT soil-moisture-triggered irrigation controller with farmer alerts via web page/mobile app. Its only reported result is that the sensor node delivers moisture readings and the pump/LED switches on and off against stored thresholds (Figure 4). No crop was grown, no yield, productivity, water use or labour data were measured; statements that the system 'improves the yield' and 'reduces human involvement' are assertions in the abstract/conclusion, not findings. Hence no own evidence on the claimed effect (enhanced agricultural productivity); the study at most supports a precondition (that the automation functions). No sites, scale, stated conditions, limitations or dispersion measures.

notes: Short conference-style paper in a low-rigour journal; much of the text appears machine-paraphrased from other sources. Figures 4 and 5 are not legible in the text, but captions indicate only sensed moisture data and the hardware set-up. Text appears complete.
